To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
tumor emboli within intramammary lymph vessels are associated with a significantly increased risk of distant metastasis, but not of local recurrence, in patients without axillary nodal metastasis.
tumor emboli in mammary lymphatics are associated with a substantial increase in the risk of distant metastasis in patients with breast carcinoma.
tumor emboli in the mammary lymphatics are associated with a high risk for distant metastases but are not associated with local recurrences in patients who have no lymph node metastases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new approaches to cancer therapy.
the development of a method of early detection of breast carcinoma.
the study of the relationship between the development of breast cancer and exposure to ionizing radiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of tumor emboli within the breast lymphatic spaces is a strong predictor for the development of distant metastases in patients with invasive mamary cancer.
tumor emboli in the lymphatics of the breast in the absence of axillary metastases are a poor prognostic indicator for patients with mammary cancer.
the finding of lymphatic emboli in patients without axillary nodal metastases is associated with a high risk of distant metastasis and a low risk of local recurrence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tumor emboli in the intramammary lymph vessels are a poor prognostic sign in patients with invasive mamary carcinoma.

the presence of intramammary tumor emboli in the primary tumor is an important prognostic factor for distant metastasis, but not for local recurrence, in patients with mamamary carcinoma without axillary lymph node metastases.

the presence of tumor cells in the lymphatic spaces of the breast, as determined by immunohistochemical analysis of lymphatic vessels in breast specimens from 38 patients with breast carcinoma, is a significant prognostic factor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of intramammary tumor emboli is associated with distant metastasis in patients with breast cancer and that this finding may have prognostic value.
the identification of tumor emboli may be a useful tool in the management of breast carcinoma.
the presence of lymphatic emboli in the breast may be used to select patients for adjuvant therapy who would otherwise be treated with surgery alone.
